India’s ‘cockroach’ movement seeks to restore culture of accountability
item.description:

India’s Cockroach Janta Party is a youth movement demanding political accountability, employment and fair elections.Read more
The founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), Abhijeet Dipke, says its goal is to restore the culture of accountability in the Indian government.
The movement, which started as online political satire, has become a major force demanding political and social change.
The CJP burst onto the political scene in May, mobilising thousands of young people to protest against exam paper leaks, unemployment and the high cost of living. Weeks later, the education minister resigned.
Now protesters have turned their attention to the chief election commissioner. They want him out.
Opposition parties and the CJP accuse India’s electoral body of manipulating voter lists in favour of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s governing Bharatiya Janata Party. The commission denies any wrongdoing. It says it was removing deceased, duplicate and ineligible voters.
The BJP has accused demonstrators of sowing chaos and trying to undermine democracy.
Dipke says that’s not true. He says the CJP wants a better India – better education, more job opportunities, free and fair elections, and for the government to stop ignoring young people.
He admits it’s a difficult fight. Several CJP leaders, including our guest, have been arrested.
But Dipke says the movement will not be shaken.Published On 8 Nov 20268 Nov 2026

Travelling supporters of Norwegian Arctic Circle club Bodo/Glimt were injured in the fall in Tromso [Ciro De Luca/Reuters]By Reuters and The Associated PressPublished On 8 Nov 20268 Nov 2026
Several fans were injured during a football match in Norway when a panel in the stand for travelling supporters gave way.
Fans fell through the hole at Tromso’s stadium and ⁠⁠⁠⁠one was taken to hospital during their match against Bodo/Glimt on Sunday, both clubs said.
The top division game was stopped just before half-time when Bodo keeper Nikita Haikin called the referee’s attention to the incident ‌‌‌‌behind the goal, where the away fans were standing in the pouring rain.
“We have had a serious incident in the away stand in connection with the game between TIL and Bodo/Glimt. Preliminary information is that a person has fallen through the stands and is injured,” Tromso said in a statement.
“Up to five people fell through ⁠⁠⁠⁠the stands and one was sent to hospital,” ⁠⁠⁠⁠Bodo press officer Simen Pedersen told the Reuters news agency.
The statement gave no details about the injuries.
“We stood and bounced to a supporter song, then the floor gave way; ⁠ ⁠⁠ ⁠it cracked in two in the row in front of us,” Andrine Moen, a Bodo supporter who witnessed the accident, told local newspaper Verdens Gang (VG).
“There were at least two ⁠⁠⁠⁠people who fell through the floor, but ⁠⁠⁠⁠we don’t know how far they fell or how many fell in total,” she said.
Bodo fans were instructed to leave the away section, with Tromso fans asked ‌‌‌‌to make space for them in other parts of the ground, VG reported.

People gather at the site where a passenger train derailed in al-Ayyat, Giza, Egypt [AP Photo]By Al Jazeera Staff, AFP and APPublished On 8 Nov 20268 Nov 2026
At least seven people have been killed and more than 112 others injured in a train crash on the outskirts of Cairo in Egypt’s Giza province, according to the country’s Health Ministry.
A train travelling between Giza and Fayoum on Sunday ran into the back of another train on the Cairo-to-Aswan route, causing the latter to derail from its tracks onto a countryside road in the district of al-Ayyat, authorities said.

Emergency rescue teams and cranes were dispatched to the scene to clear the wreckage and restore train services to their normal schedule as soon as possible, Egyptian National Railways said.
Authorities say more than 70 ambulances were involved in transport and evacuation operations at the scene of the crash, with casualties taken to nearby hospitals.
Previous accidents
Al-Ayyat district, where the collision happened, is also the site of Egypt’s worst-ever rail disaster.
In 2002, more than 370 people were killed when a fire swept through a train carrying holiday travellers south of Cairo. In 2009, multiple train crashes in the area killed dozens.
Egypt’s 110 million people depend heavily on rail transport, but the cross-country network – one of the largest in Africa – is in need of modernisation.

Abed Abou Shhadeh was held for five days without charge in a Shin Bet intelligence facility in Petah Tikva, on the outskirts of Tel Aviv. [Courtesy of Abed Abou Shhadeh]By Al Jazeera StaffPublished On 8 Nov 20268 Nov 2026
Israeli authorities have released Palestinian journalist Abed Abou Shhadeh after detaining him for five days without charge.
Speaking after his release, Abou Shhadeh said on Sunday that his detention was part of “political measures” intended not only for him “but to intimidate Arab society as a whole”.

“In my view, the most appropriate response is to reaffirm among ourselves that we are on the right side, that our path is the path of truth,” he said, adding that he would continue his work as a journalist.
Abou Shhadeh was held in a Shin Bet intelligence facility in Petah Tikva, on the outskirts of Tel Aviv, after being detained on Tuesday on suspicion of “contact with a foreign agent”.
He was suspected of receiving money from foreign sources in order to support Israel’s Arab voters, according to the legal rights group Adalah, which is part of his defence team.
The accusation came after Abou Shhadeh, a Palestinian citizen of Israel, spoke on the al-Midan podcast for the Arab48 website and appeared as an analyst on Al Jazeera.
He addressed topics similar to those discussed in Israeli media outlets, according to Hadeel Abu Salih, his legal counsel and a human rights lawyer with Adalah.

Tenerife football club bids farewell to Jesus de MiguelBy Leyla HamedPublished On 8 Nov 20268 Nov 2026
A bouquet of flowers marked the spot on the pitch where Jesus De Miguel fell five days earlier. His teammates returned to the stadium dressed in all black. Above them hung a banner that read “Eterno Demi 9” – Demi 9 forever – a reference to the number nine’s nickname.
In the stands, supporters chanted the name they had once roared to celebrate his goals for CD Tenerife. On Saturday, it was a wail to bid him goodbye.
Thousands gathered at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium in Santa Cruz, the capital of Tenerife in the Spanish Canary Islands, where the forward suffered a collision on Monday that resulted in his tragic death. Silence gave way to applause before the club’s centenary anthem was played.Flowers and a shirt are placed on the pitch where striker Jesus de Miguel fell after a collision [Borja Suarez/Reuters]
‘Tremendously unfair’
On the makeshift stage, captain Enric Gallego struggled through his farewell speech.
He recalled a teammate so reluctant to inconvenience others that, when his car broke down, he walked home without asking for help.
“To speak of you in the past tense is tremendously unfair,” Gallego said, pausing to regain composure.
“It’s still hard to believe that this has happened to us, Demi, ⁠⁠⁠you’ll always be one of us. We’re still struggling to come to terms with the fact that you won’t be with us again.” ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌Tenerife’s Enric Gallego holds back his tears during his tribute speech [Borja Suarez/Reuters]
